What is a consent decree? Meaning and recent DOJ cases. A consent decree is a court-approved settlement in which two parties resolve a dispute without either side admitting guilt or liability. The court keeps oversight of how the agreement is carried out. The term is most often used in the United States, and federal courts use it to enforce laws on antitrust, employment discrimination and environmental rules.. Harmeet Dhillon, the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division chief, resigned on Thursday after about 18 months in the post. Once a judge signs it, the terms carry the force of a court order, and a violation can lead to further court action. The term came up in the news this week when Harmeet Dhillon, assistant attorney general in charge of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division, resigned on Thursday, according to Attorney General Todd Blanche. Under her leadership, the division dismissed more than 50 long-standing consent decrees with public school systems, many in the Deep South, that had protected Black students from unlawful discrimination. What is a game-time decision? Meaning in the NFL injury report. What is a game-time decision? It is an injury status meaning a player's availability will not be settled until shortly before kickoff.
